saw.short: Bradley Walsh's new Channel 4 quiz has viewers guessing
saw.headline: Bradley Walsh's new quiz has *viewers guessing*
saw.what: Channel 4 has advertised “The Million Pound Shot”, due Sunday at 9pm, with a trailer only on live TV. Viewers recorded and shared it online. The only detail is a TV guide line: three contestants, £1m and “one huge secret twist”. Channel 4 hasn't released details.
saw.why: A mystery drop turns viewers into the marketing. People guess before anything is confirmed.

saw.short: Netflix's new Pride and Prejudice trailer lands
saw.headline: Netflix's new *Pride and Prejudice* trailer lands
saw.what: Netflix released a new Pride and Prejudice trailer on Wednesday, with Emma Corrin as Lizzie, Jack Lowden as Darcy and Olivia Colman as Mrs Bennet, who gets the opening line. The six-part series is reported for 3 Dec.
saw.why: Fans pick period dramas apart frame by frame. Even Mr Collins's sideburns are getting attention, per Metro.

saw.short: The niche Halloween costume meme is back
saw.headline: The *niche Halloween costume* meme is back
saw.what: The annual format is back on X: people caption deep-cut costume ideas, such as Dakota Johnson and limes or Princess Diana's revenge dress. The Tab, citing Know Your Meme, traces it to 2022–2023, and it went massively viral in 2024.
saw.why: The more obscure the costume, the better the post. Brands can play with deep cuts from their own world.

saw.short: Firefox reunites YouTube-era meme legends in an ad
saw.headline: Firefox reunites *YouTube-era meme legends* in an ad
saw.what: Firefox posted a one-minute ad on 25 Oct with Numa Numa guy, Chuck Testa, Overly Attached Girlfriend, Annoying Orange and Tay Zonday, asking “What happened to the internet?” Dexerto reports 8m+ views.
saw.why: Nostalgia sells. Real internet characters beat a mascot when the joke is shared memory.

saw.short: A Walmart x Disney Muppets Christmas ad kicks off ad season
saw.headline: A Walmart × Disney *Muppets Christmas ad* kicks off ad season
saw.what: Walmart's US ad “A Who Knew Carol”, made with Disney and The Muppets Studio, riffs on The Muppet Christmas Carol, with Walton Goggins as Scrooge. It ends by teasing three more ghosts: Christmas Presents, Deals to Come and Christmas Fast. It's a US campaign.
saw.why: Christmas ads are starting, and this one borrows a Disney classic. Watch for UK launches.

saw.short: U2 announce a secret BBC gig for 3 Nov
saw.headline: U2 announce a *secret BBC gig* for 3 Nov
saw.what: Jo Whiley announced on Radio 2 that U2 will play an exclusive BBC show at a secret central London venue on Tuesday 3 Nov. Free tickets are by BBC Audiences ballot, which closes tonight. It airs on Radio 2 and BBC Sounds on 30 Nov.
saw.why: A surprise gig with a ballot gets people posting to win. Guessing the venue is part of the fun.

platform.short: Meta launches kids' AI apps, but not in the UK
platform.headline: Meta launches *kids' AI apps*, but not in the UK
platform.what: Meta has launched “Waddle World”, a 16-bit pet game whose pet remembers what users say, and “Style Sketch”, which builds outfits from users' clothes. Social Media Today reports Waddle World is only in the Philippines, and Style Sketch only in Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand.
platform.why: Parents will ask about kids and AI apps. Neither is available in the UK yet.

platform.headline: YouTube says *microdramas* passed 6.5bn views
platform.what: YouTube says microdramas, short serialised dramas, passed 6.5bn views in the first half of 2026, up more than 50% on last year. It will also revamp members-only episodes on mobile in the coming weeks. The figure first came out in September.
platform.why: Serialised short stories are a format brands can borrow. The numbers are YouTube's own.

platform.short: X lets you re-share photos with credit
platform.headline: X lets you *re-share photos with credit*
platform.what: On X you can long-press a photo and tap “Post photo”. The original author gets a credit link, and both accounts earn under Original Content Rewards, which is for Premium accounts. UK availability isn't stated.
platform.why: Reposting other people's photos with credit is now built in. Check eligibility before relying on it.
